one_line: A scholar from Ghazni and a Rajput court bard, personifying how medieval India was remembered in careful observation and heroic song.

appearance.age_look: al-Biruni appears in his late 40s with a medium build; Chand Bardai appears in his late 30s with a lean, wiry build.
appearance.face: al-Biruni has an oval face, light wheat complexion, short neatly trimmed beard, straight nose, thoughtful sharp eyes and a calm, slightly serious default expression; Chand Bardai has a longer face, warm brown complexion, trimmed moustache, faint stubble, strong nose, and bright, animated eyes with a quietly proud default half-smile.
appearance.hair: al-Biruni’s dark brown hair is mostly hidden under a soft rounded white cloth cap wrapped with a muted teal turban band, with short hair at the nape visible; Chand Bardai has shoulder-length black hair parted in the middle, smoothed back and tied low, with a simple narrow maroon cloth band around his head like a minimalist pagri strip.
appearance.costume: al-Biruni wears an 11th-century Khurasani scholar’s outfit: a long, ankle-length off-white cotton robe with narrow vertical weave texture, straight sleeves to the wrist, and a simple round neckline, over which he has a loose knee-length teal woolen outer coat (aba-style) with open front and a subtle darker teal border; a wide plain brown leather belt wraps his waist, and he wears loose sand-colored trousers tucked neatly into soft brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; Chand Bardai wears a late-medieval north Indian bardic court ensemble: a knee-length, side-tied angarkha of soft cream cotton with fine red edging at the collar, overlap and cuffs, tied with thin interior ties, over a deep indigo dhoti wrapped tightly and brought between the legs in the Marwar style, ending at the ankles; he has a light maroon cotton patka (scarf) folded as a sash diagonally across his torso from left shoulder to right hip, with a faint woven geometric pattern, and simple dark brown leather sandals with toe loops, plus a modest copper armlet on one upper arm and a thin beaded thread bracelet on one wrist.
appearance.signature: al-Biruni carries a medium-sized dark brown leather-bound codex tucked under one arm, with a visible cloth bookmark and a small wooden geometric astrolabe-like disk hanging from his belt; Chand Bardai carries a short wooden harp-like veena (small folk lute) with a gourd resonator and two main strings, slung on his back by a simple rope strap, and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with red string at his waist.

ref_desc: Depict al-Biruni as a late-40s Khurasani scholar with light wheat complexion, white cap with teal band, off-white robe, teal coat, brown belt and book with astrolabe, alongside Chand Bardai, a late-30s Rajput bard with warm brown skin, tied shoulder-length hair, cream angarkha, indigo dhoti, maroon sash, sandals and a small lute with manuscript, in a teal, maroon, indigo and brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historically grounded characters standing side by side: al-Biruni, a late-40s Khurasani scholar with an oval light wheat face, short trimmed beard and thoughtful eyes, wearing a soft rounded white cloth cap wrapped with a muted teal band, a long ankle-length off-white cotton robe with subtle vertical texture and straight sleeves, a loose knee-length teal woolen open-front coat with a slightly darker teal border, a wide plain brown leather belt, loose sand-colored trousers and soft brown leather shoes with gently upturned toes; a medium-sized dark brown leather-bound book is tucked under his arm and a small wooden geometric astrolabe-like disk hangs from his belt. Next to him, Chand Bardai, a late-30s Rajput bard with a longer warm brown face, bright expressive eyes, trimmed moustache and faint stubble, has straight black hair parted in the middle and tied low at the back with a narrow maroon cloth headband; he wears a knee-length cream cotton angarkha tied at the side with fine red edging on collar and cuffs, a deep indigo dhoti wrapped in Marwar style to the ankles, a light maroon cotton patka worn diagonally from left shoulder to right hip with a subtle geometric weave, simple dark brown leather sandals with toe loops, a modest copper armlet and a thin beaded thread bracelet; a small wooden harp-like lute with a gourd resonator hangs on his back by a rope strap, and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with red string is tucked at his waist. Use a harmonious palette of off-white, teal, maroon, indigo and brown leather tones, and show front-facing, slight profile and rear views to clarify the fixed face, hair, clothing and props.
